
The five chains in `record-forms.json` recreate structural measurements from authorised crew records: a task-notice enqueue followed by a textless dequeue as the next queue-operation, strictly later and within one second; a failed task notice stamped between its Bash invocation and handle result; an error-string result of an explicit background invocation that created no task; a successful local_bash TaskStop naming a known Monitor; and an old resume-stopped task. Identities, times, commands, summaries, outputs and ordinary prompts are synthetic. No crew record is included. The dequeue classifier carries forward only the preceding measured notice's identity, not arbitrary queue contents. A separate invocation timestamp validates early notices; the task's displayed start remains its later handle acknowledgement.

Separate throwaway captures on 2.1.317 and 2.1.325 proved a live background sleep dead after retirement of its owning program window, and still dead after resume. Both emitted killed notices; resume also emitted the exact existing stopped/no-completion note. A launch-scoped reader view may therefore mark an old pending or exact resume-stopped task `ended-by-relaunch` when all of its execution evidence predates the current launch. That state never claims successful completion and never changes the cached native evidence. Unknown versions, invalid tasks, conflicting evidence and current-launch activity remain held.
